To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) humans and machines struggle with a synthetic visual challenge, PathTracker, that requires tracking objects based on their motion trajectories; 2) we introduce a circuit model that captures the visual strategies used by humans to solve PathTracker and show that this model can be used in a transformer architecture for object tracking in natural scenes; and 3) our work highlights the importance and benefits of understanding human vision for improving computer vision.
